columns.projection: the input's value, decoded and returned: Go, Python and Rust must write the same canonical bytes (escapes, key order, integers)
[kind, pos, end, parent reference] of every node of the plain walk (ForEachChild preorder; reparsed nodes included, JSDoc comments not), read in setup; the column only returns them

[kind, pos, end, parent reference] of every node of the JSDoc walk (the plain walk with each node's own JSDoc comments and their subtrees before its children; a comment a reparsed declaration shares is visited under its parent only), read in setup; the column only returns them
[node reference, symbol key, symbol flags] of every node whose Node.Symbol is not nil after binding, read in setup; the column only returns them
[node reference, symbol key, symbol flags] of every node whose Node.Symbol is not nil after binding, under the JSDoc walk, read in setup; the column only returns them

notes: The harness's own columns: they claim no operation and show that the Go and Rust setups (both document-order walks, binding and symbol keys) agree before any column's value is compared.
